meta.title: AMDL: Apple Music to your own disk, lossless and tagged
meta.description: AMDL is a self-hosted, open-source downloader. Paste an Apple Music link or search the catalog, and it saves finished, tagged .m4a files: ALAC up to 24-bit/192 kHz, Dolby Atmos or AAC. Use it from a web console, the desktop app, a terminal, or an AI agent over MCP.
meta.ogAlt: AMDL: Apple Music, on your own disk.

hero.title:
Apple Music,
on your own disk.
hero.lead: Paste a song, album, playlist, artist or station link, or search the catalog. AMDL downloads, decrypts, remuxes and tags every track into a finished `.m4a`, and keeps a record of what is on your disk.
hero.fine: AGPL-3.0 · macOS, Windows, Linux and Docker
hero.strip: One track's waveform in four parts, one for each stage, ending in a tagged .m4a file

product.title: Search it, queue it, keep it.
product.lead: Three screens of the web console and the desktop app, drawn by hand with made-up music. Each one has a button that works.

search.label: Search
search.text: Songs, albums, artists and playlists from Apple's catalog, with the formats each one comes in.

queue.label: Queue
queue.text: One row per album or playlist. The running one shows each track's stage; failed tracks retry on their own.

library.label: Library
library.text: The record of an album: every track, every quality, and where its file is.

product.note: Illustrations: the albums and artists are made up, and nothing is downloaded.

queue.label: An illustration of the Queue: one album running, two queued, one done and one failed

specs.title: The parts you would otherwise script.
specs.lead: One server keeps the queue, the records of what you own and the folder they live in, and runs them for you.

formats.text: List the codecs you want, in order. Each gets its own retries; when one runs out, the next takes over, with AAC-LC as the last resort.

records.text: Each album and playlist is kept per track and per quality. A failed track is retried by later runs on its own, and a disk check finds files that went missing.
records.label: Twelve tracks of a record: ten downloaded, one waiting to retry, one missing

library.text: Songs, albums and artists share one folder tree, laid out by a template. A file already in place is adopted, not downloaded again.

accounts.text: A wrapper-manager holds up to ten Apple Music accounts. A link is read in its own region's catalog when one of them serves it.

lyrics.text: Tags, cover art and lyrics go into the file: LRC timed by line or by word, with translation and romanization if you want them.

automation.text: Call a webhook or run a command when a job is queued or ends, for example to refresh your media server. Library sync downloads the album behind each song you add in Apple Music.

agents.text: Every result is JSON on stdout and every error has its own exit status. `amdl mcp` serves the same commands as MCP tools, and none of them signs in, so a password never passes through a model.

run.title: One core, four ways in.
run.lead: Every product runs on the same Go core. Deploy the server once, then use whichever fits the moment.

server.title: Server and web console
server.text: `amdl serve`: one Go process with SQLite, a REST and Server-Sent Events API under `/api/v1`, and the console on the same port. Jobs survive a restart; images for amd64 and arm64 are on GHCR.

desktop.title: Desktop app
desktop.text: A native app for macOS, Windows and Linux, drawn with MyGo: a client of your server, or a backend of its own. It ships with 2.0, and its packages are not signed yet: [installing it]({blob}/docs/install.md#the-desktop-app).

terminal.title: CLI and TUI
terminal.text: `amdl` on its own opens an interactive interface: paste a link, or type to search. `amdl service install` runs the backend on this machine, starting at login.

agents.title: AI agents
agents.text: `amdl cli setup` prints the MCP config a coding agent needs. From a search to a download takes two tools, `search_catalog` and `start_download`.

install.title: Up and running in a few minutes.
install.lead: You need an Apple Music subscription and a wrapper: the service that holds your Apple Music login. Run the wrapper on a Linux box, or let amdl run it on your own machine: natively on Linux x86_64, in a QEMU guest elsewhere.

steps.title: Install amdl
steps.text: The script checks the release against its `SHA256SUMS` and puts `amdl` in `~/.local/bin`, printing the line to add to `PATH` if that folder is not on it. On Windows it goes to your user programs folder.

steps.title: Check ffmpeg
steps.text: Every track goes through ffmpeg. `amdl doctor` says whether this machine has it, and prints the command that installs it if not.

steps.title: Get a wrapper
steps.text: This downloads the wrapper guest AMDL-Web publishes and checks it against a pinned hash; on Linux x86_64 it runs the wrapper natively, elsewhere it needs QEMU, which it offers to install. Already run a wrapper on a NAS or server? Skip this step.

steps.title: Run the backend
steps.text: This registers the backend as a service that starts at login, and it starts the wrapper with it. For a wrapper elsewhere, add `--wrapper <its address>`. `amdl service status` prints the console's address: sign in on its Account page, or here with `amdl wrapper login`.

steps.title: Get the Compose file
steps.text: In an empty directory. It runs the image `ghcr.io/amdl-web/apple-music-downloader`. Create `data/downloads` first and give it to the backend's user (`PUID:PGID`, 1000:1000 unless you set them); otherwise Docker creates it as root.

steps.title: Turn on the wrapper
steps.text: In `docker-compose.yml`, uncomment the `wrapper-manager` service and the `volumes:` block at the end of the file.

steps.title: Start both
steps.text: Compose builds wrapper-manager from its v2 branch, so the host needs internet access.

steps.title: Point at the wrapper and sign in
steps.text: Open `http://localhost:18080/`, go to **Settings › Account**, set **Session service** to the address below, save and restart from the notice. Then sign in with your Apple ID and paste a link into **New download**; finished files land in `./data/downloads`.

nas.label: NAS
nas.text: The wrapper needs user namespaces: `unshare -Ur true` must succeed. On a host without them, such as Synology DSM, use wrapper-manager v2's QEMU variant, which needs `/dev/kvm`.

install.more: Every option of both paths is in the [install guide]({blob}/docs/install.md) and the [deployment guide]({blob}/docs/deployment.md). Coming from 1.x? Read [upgrading to 2.0]({blob}/docs/upgrading-to-2.0.md) first.

notice: AMDL needs your own Apple Music subscription and is for personal use: each install serves one person. It relies on Apple's undocumented web-player API, which can change without notice.
